signals.signal: HNB Tables PI1/PI3 (published 27/05/2026): at 31/03/2026 Croatia had 4,054 ATMs, 161,922 EFTPOS terminals, 778 bank operating units, 423 cash-withdrawal terminals, 367 day/night deposit boxes and 41 coin-deposit machines. ATMs grew 3,787 (31/01/2026) to 4,054 (31/03/2026), +267 in two months. Only 2,110 of 4,054 ATMs are contactless+contact; 1,939 are contact-only.
signals.source_name: Hrvatska narodna banka - Statistics / Payment services / Infrastructure, Tables PI1 and PI3
signals.implies: Fleet expanding fast and nearly half still contact-only, i.e. an installed base due for contactless/NFC replacement or upgrade. Direct pipeline for Printec ATM/self-service hardware, contactless retrofit and managed services; 41 coin-deposit machines means coin automation is almost untouched.
signals.likelihood: High - counts already rising month on month
signals.followup: Pull PI2 (county split) and monthly PI1 updates through 2026 and attribute the +267 to individual banks

signals.signal: Croatia's consumer-fee law obliges every bank to offer a free basic services package. MoF Q&A dated 04/02/2026 confirms the package must include free cash DEPOSIT to the account at a counter or ATM (coin processing explicitly excluded) and free withdrawal at the account-holding bank's own ATM; from 01/01/2027 a package holder also gets two free monthly withdrawals at OTHER banks' ATMs in Croatia. The bank's response deadline on a customer request falls from 30 days to 10 working days on 02/07/2026.
signals.source_name: Ministarstvo financija RH - Pitanja i odgovori (paket besplatnih usluga), PDF
signals.implies: Making ATM cash DEPOSIT free by law pushes deposit volume off the teller onto machines - a direct demand driver for deposit ATMs and recyclers (Printec cash automation), branch transformation and managed cash services. The coin carve-out flags coin-deposit machines as a chargeable add-on.
signals.followup: Get the Zakon text and Narodne novine citation; track deposit-ATM additions per bank since 01/01/2026

signals.entity: Croatia - national shared ATM network project
signals.signal: Banks must stand up an interoperable national ATM network by 01/01/2027 or be forced to give non-customers two free withdrawals per month. Ernst & Young was commissioned to design the scheme and produced three operating models; the Croatian Banking Association calls it technically, operationally and legally complex. Finance Minister Marko Primorac said in late May 2026 no agreement had been reached and that banks have about a year and a half to decide. FINA was originally floated as operator but responsibility shifted to the banks. Reported context: 3,816 active ATMs in 2024 rising above 4,700 by summer, 106 million ATM transactions worth EUR 19.24bn a year.
signals.source_name: tportal - 'Sprema se velika promjena na bankomatima: ceka se samo jedan dogovor'
signals.implies: A pooled national ATM utility is the single biggest Croatian opportunity in this cluster: it needs a multivendor switch/driving layer, shared monitoring, cash forecasting/optimisation (OptiCash-class) and an outsourced ATM-as-a-service operator - exactly Printec's managed-services proposition. The 01/01/2027 statutory backstop forces a decision within 6 months.
signals.likelihood: High that a decision lands before 01/01/2027
signals.followup: Find the EY three models, the Government/HNB/HUB memorandum, and whether an operator RFP exists; monitor HUB and HNB statements

signals.signal: OTP banka Hrvatska's own public locator on 31/07/2026 lists 460 ATMs, of which 353 are withdrawal-only ('Isplatni bankomat') and only 107 are deposit-and-withdrawal ('Uplatno-isplatni bankomat'), and 95 branches. That compares with the OTP Group disclosure of 442 ATMs / 99 branches at 31/03/2026, i.e. roughly +18 ATMs and -4 branches in four months. The bank's own page states clients have 'over 470 ATMs'. The Djakovo branch closed on 15/07/2026, with customers redirected to Nasice and other Osjecko-baranjska county branches.
signals.source_name: OTP banka Hrvatska - Bankomati and Poslovnice locator (print view)
signals.implies: 77% of OTP HR's fleet is still withdrawal-only while branches shrink and the law makes ATM deposit free - a textbook recycler/deposit-ATM upgrade case. Printec already services OTP Group's Croatian NCR/Atleos fleet (OTP HR plus former Splitska), so this is a defend-and-expand play: recycler swap-out, cash-cycle optimisation and managed services.
signals.likelihood: High - branch closures plus free-ATM-deposit law force deposit automation
signals.followup: Confirm OEM mix and contract renewal dates for the OTP HR fleet; pitch a recycler conversion programme for the 353 withdrawal-only units

signals.signal: Erste Croatia's own branch/ATM API (local.erstebank.hr/api/v1) returned on 31/07/2026: 666 ATMs, of which only 199 are deposit-capable and 161 sit inside branches - so 467 units (70%) are withdrawal-only; and 106 branches, of which 97 have a cash desk and 94 offer advisory/consultation.
signals.source_name: Erste&Steiermaerkische Bank - Poslovnice i bankomati locator API (local.erstebank.hr/api/v1/atms, /branches)
signals.implies: Erste HR runs the largest disclosed non-UniCredit ATM fleet in Croatia and 70% of it cannot take deposits. With free ATM deposit now a legal entitlement, Erste has to convert a large slice to recyclers - a big cash-automation and cash-forecasting (OptiCash-class) opportunity, plus branch-transformation self-service zones for the 97 cash-desk branches.
signals.followup: Confirm the OEM of the 666 units and whether Erste HR runs OptiCash or an Erste Group-standard cash-management tool; check Erste Group ATM procurement framework

signals.signal: Podravska banka's unaudited H1-2026 report, filed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange EHO on 28/07/2026, shows total assets of EUR 748.1m at 30/06/2026 (down from EUR 767.8m at 31/12/2025), 220 employees, and a profit for the period of EUR 2,569,963 against a full-year 2025 loss of EUR 2,471,338. Separately, POBA filed voting-rights change notifications on 06/05/2026 and again on 11/06/2026, following the 04/05/2026 disclosure of the obligation to publish a takeover bid after AikGroup contracted to buy 613,567 shares (91.75%) at EUR 68.7851 per share.
signals.source_name: Zagreb Stock Exchange EHO - PODRAVSKA BANKA d.d. issuer announcements (Q2-2026 financial report; voting-rights notifications)
signals.implies: A small bank returning to profit and about to change owner. AikGroup/AIK Banka is a regional consolidator with its own technology standards; post-closing IT and channel harmonisation (ATM/self-service, card and POS switching, AML/compliance, eKYC) is the entry point. Printec should treat a Croatian AikGroup entity as a new logo alongside its existing Serbian AIK relationships.
signals.followup: Obtain the 11/06/2026 voting-rights PDF (scanned, no text layer - needs OCR or manual read) to confirm whether AikGroup's stake has actually transferred; check HANFA takeover-offer register and HNB/ECB qualifying-holding approvals

signals.signal: Zagrebacka banka reported H1-2026 post-tax profit of EUR 251m at bank level, down EUR 7m or 2.7% year on year, and EUR 301m at group level, down EUR 4m or 1.3%. Operating income EUR 417m (+0.7%), operating costs EUR 118m (+0.9%), cost/income ratio 28.30%. Net interest income EUR 278m; net fee and commission income jumped 16% to EUR 109m.
signals.source_name: tportal - 'Zaba u prvom polugodistu imala dobit od 251 milijun eura'
signals.implies: Fee income growing 16% while interest income flattens is exactly the profile that funds transaction-technology investment: card/POS acquiring, self-service and digital channels. A 28.3% cost/income ratio also means ZABA can afford, and will be pushed toward, self-service/branch automation. Printec angle: ATM/self-service, POS and managed services into the largest Croatian bank.
signals.followup: Get ZABA's own H1-2026 report from zaba.hr investor pages for branch/ATM counts and any self-service capex commentary
